overview: This bill, the Closing the Provider Fraud Gap Act, directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO), Congress's nonpartisan watchdog agency, to study how well fraud is prevented among providers in federal early childhood programs. It covers Head Start, the Child and Adult Care Food Program (which pays for meals at child care centers and day care homes), and the Child Care and Development Block Grant program, the main federal program that gives states money to help low-income families pay for child care. The study must look at whether current safeguards work, whether the data the government collects is enough to spot fraud and is actually used, and how states that hand off child care program management to counties or other local bodies are doing. GAO must report its findings and any recommendations to Congress within two years. As of April 6, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say an independent review will show where fraud prevention in child care and nutrition programs is falling short so Congress can target fixes and protect taxpayer money.
against: Critics say a study alone does not stop fraud and that Congress could act on problems already known instead of waiting two years for a report.
